lines.text: Buy you a coffee, not invite!
Many learners say: I will invite you a coffee.
Better: I will buy you a coffee.
Invite means ask someone to come.
Buy! Let me buy you lunch.

data.wrong: I will invite you a coffee.
data.right: I will buy you a coffee.
data.why: Invite means ask someone to come.

native.tip: En español “te invito un café”, pero en inglés “invite” es pedir que alguien venga. Para pagar: “buy you a coffee.”

en.tip: In Spanish “te invito un café” is normal, but English “invite” means ask someone to come. To pay, say “buy you a coffee.”
